title: Chapter 87: You Are Inside the Drawing
html:
Someone had carved the words into the table with the tip of a pen. Every stroke bit deep into the wood, testifying to the writer’s pain and desperation. The lines clustered at the center. Chen Ge bent closer to read them.

“The eyes on the toilet wall came alive! I saw it, the eyes were moving!”

“I don’t know why I imagined it, but ever since that day, I’ve felt a pair of eyes following me.”

“They could be hiding anywhere—inside a drawer, under the bed, behind my pillow.”

“I’m afraid even to look inside my bag. What if a pair of eyes looks back?”

“I’m afraid of being alone. I can’t enter tight spaces. I’m terrified of the dark. The instant the lights go out, I wake from nightmares screaming. I think I’ve lost my mind, and those eyes are watching me spiral into madness.”

“What should I do? A pair of eyes is following me.”

“They must be hiding somewhere, and they look familiar, but I cannot place them.”

“I told my parents and homeroom teacher, but they brushed me off. They said I was probably studying too hard.”

“They’re probably right. I must be exhausted. Why else would I think those eyes look exactly like my teacher’s?”

“My parents asked the teacher to keep an eye on me. I know they meant well, but whenever he comes close, I want to grab a pen and stab out his eyes.”

“Have I finally lost my mind? I don’t dare tell anyone else. I’m afraid of the eyes, and I’m afraid people will call me crazy.”

“I pretend to laugh and smile as before, but I see the eyes more and more often. I don’t know whom to trust.”

“I’m falling apart. Needles and fruit knives put terrible thoughts in my head. Sometimes I start sobbing for no reason. I want the tears to stop, but I can’t control them. I know they’re watching.”

“This can’t continue. I only want to be free.”

“I hope the rumors about this classroom are real. I am willing to give up everything just to destroy that pair of eyes.”

After reading the account, Chen Ge did not rush away. He carefully recorded every line on his livestream, preserving the evidence. The words appeared to have been carved by the girl Teacher Fan had victimized.

The eyes in the toilet had traumatized her. Together with Teacher Fan’s other abuse, they drove her to seek help from the cursed classroom. After she paid its price, Fan Yu’s parents disappeared. In a sense, the eyes haunting her had been destroyed.

The sealed classroom had played a crucial role. Teacher Fan’s true killers might have been the things residing within it.

The three notes were written in different hands by people absent from the student roster, people capable of killing. If the classroom’s ghosts were responsible, they fit every condition.

Chen Ge looked around, his resolve wavering as he remembered the group photograph Fan Yu’s aunt had shown him. He might be facing far more than one or two ghosts. Perhaps an entire class was trapped there.

Chen Ge inspected the other desks. Words had been carved into every one.

Every table has words carved into it, all in different hands.

As Chen Ge approached the next desk, he bumped the one holding the textbook, paper, and pen. The pen rolled over the edge and fell.

Chen Ge bent to retrieve it, but an arm reached from beside the desk, picked up the pen, and handed it to him.

“Thank you.” Chen Ge accepted it on reflex. As he straightened to return the pen to the desk, he froze. A chill surged up his spine.

Where did the arm come from?

He swung his mallet toward where the arm had been, but struck only air. The sealed classroom looked unchanged; every table and chair remained where it had been. Chen Ge, however, now saw the room differently.

There’s a classroom at the end of the corridor that’s always sealed. No one ever enters it, but every night, it comes alive with activity. And it’s almost midnight.

The mission description flashed through his mind and made him shudder. Side mission be damned—he wanted out of the classroom as quickly as possible.

The closer he came to the door, the more anxious he grew. He expected it to slam shut at the last instant, leaving him to turn and find the classroom filled with ‘people.’ He quickened his pace and rushed through. Mercifully, nothing happened.

This side mission may be impossible.Looking back at the classroom, Chen Ge accepted that the rumors were probably true. An entire class had become ghosts and remained there.

He closed the classroom door, but before he could catch his breath, something on the floor stopped him cold. A second set of footprints stood beside his own. Their owner had lingered before the classroom, then walked away.

These look like the prints of rubber shoes; this person came prepared.

Someone had watched through the window while he investigated the sealed classroom. Fear tightened Chen Ge’s chest. If the ghosts had driven him toward the exit, that person could easily have locked the door from outside.

Gripping the mallet in his hand, Chen Ge soon calmed down. Footprints can’t be hidden that easily. I’ll need to find this person first before I decide what to do.

He followed the trail. The other person had made no attempt to hide it; the prints lay clear and distinct, almost inviting pursuit. They led to the third-floor toilet. Chen Ge put away his phone and slowly pushed open the door.

A woman in a raincoat stood before the fifth cubicle. Slender and frail, she looked ready to collapse at any moment.

“Human or ghost, you’re not leaving until you explain yourself.” Chen Ge kept three meters between them.

At last, the woman lowered her hood. “I never expected you to come here. I’m here to save you.”

The woman who appeared at Mu Yang High School at midnight was Fan Yu’s aunt.

“Save me?” Chen Ge did not believe her fully. Fan Yu’s aunt was still a suspect. He had not forgotten about the woman’s insistence on giving him that glass of water.

“Yes. I saw Fan Yu’s drawing.” The woman pulled a crumpled sheet of paper from inside her raincoat. “You’re in it.”

“Place it on the floor and take a few steps back.”

Fan Yu’s aunt dropped the drawing and retreated to stand beside the sixth cubicle.
